title: What is Method Overloading?
description: Explain how method overloading works in Java.

section-content: Method overloading happens when multiple methods share the same name.
The methods must differ by parameter list.
question-content.section-text: Overloading allows one method name to perform similar tasks with different inputs.

hints: Methods can have the same name

solution-list.description: Method overloading lets you define multiple methods with the same name as long as their parameters are different.

thread.comment: How can Java tell the methods apart?

replies.comment: Because the parameter lists are different.

title: What is a HashSet?
description: Describe what a HashSet is and when to use it.

section-content: A HashSet stores unique elements only.
It does not guarantee insertion order.
It is useful when duplicates should be removed.
question-content.section-text: A HashSet is a collection that prevents duplicate values.

hints: Think about a collection of unique values

solution-list.description: A HashSet is useful when you want a collection of values with no duplicates and fast membership checks.

thread.comment: Can I add the same value twice?

title: What is an ArrayList?
description: Explain how ArrayList works in Java.

section-content: It allows adding and removing elements.
It is part of java.util package.

solution-list.description: ArrayList allows dynamic resizing unlike normal arrays.

section-content: Recursion is when a method calls itself.
It requires a base case to stop.
Used in problems like factorial or tree traversal.
question-content.section-text: Recursion breaks problems into smaller pieces.

solution-list.description: Recursion solves problems by calling the same function with smaller inputs.

replies.comment: Yes, factorial is a great example.

title: Binary Search Tree: Validate BST
description: Given the root of a binary tree, determine whether it is a valid Binary Search Tree. A valid BST requires every left subtree node to be strictly less than its root, every right subtree node to be strictly greater, and both subtrees must also be valid BSTs.

section-content: A valid BST has all left nodes less than the root.
All right nodes must be greater than the root.
Both subtrees must also be valid BSTs.
question-content.section-text: Use recursive bounds to validate each node.

hints: Pass min and max bounds as you recurse
Use Long.MIN_VALUE and Long.MAX_VALUE as starting bounds
Going left updates the upper bound

solution-list.description: Recursively validate each node by passing down min and max bounds. Going left tightens the upper bound, going right tightens the lower bound.

title: Binary Search Tree: Lowest Common Ancestor
description: Given the root of a BST and two node values p and q, find their Lowest Common Ancestor. The LCA is the deepest node that has both p and q as descendants, where a node counts as a descendant of itself.

section-content: The LCA is the deepest shared ancestor of two nodes.
BST ordering helps narrow the search direction.
If both values are less than root go left, if both greater go right.
question-content.section-text: Exploit BST ordering to find where the two nodes diverge.

hints: Use BST ordering to decide direction
If both values are smaller than root go left
The first node where p and q split is the LCA

solution-list.description: Iterate through the BST using its ordering property. If both targets are smaller go left, if both are larger go right, otherwise the current node is the LCA.
